title: 2026-03-03 QBR - Bluewave Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Discussed optimization opportunities (batching, quantization), dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and a proposed pilot for private deployment benchmarks. Agreed next steps: pricing recap, security pack, and a performance benchmark run next week.
topics: Usage and cost trends: tokens, embeddings, peak patterns
Reliability: recent 03/01 incident, error rates, SLA adherence
Optimization recommendations: batching, prefix caching, model quantization
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
Roadmap alignment and pilot scope for 1-month performance run
action_items: Tom Nguyen — Share peak-hour request logs and sample traces — Due: 2026-03-06
Diego Ramos — Run targeted benchmark (p50/p95/p99) with Bluewave sample prompt set on dedicated nodes — Due: 2026-03-10
Priya Singh — Send updated pricing worksheet and recommended batching settings — Due: 2026-03-05
Maya Chen — Share SOC2/ISO pack and private deployment checklist — Due: 2026-03-04
next_steps: Schedule 60-min benchmark run (Redwood SE + Bluewave infra) for week of 2026-03-08
Redwood to provide a one-month pilot proposal and sample SOW
Bluewave to confirm stakeholder list for pilot (security, infra, product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 45 minutes scheduled, hope that's still good with folks.
[00:06] Aisha: Yep, all good, appreciate you doing the QBR.
[00:10] Priya: Quick agenda — usage/costs, reliability incidents, optimization recs, and pilot next steps.
[00:18] Tom: Sounds good, we'll kick off with the numbers from our side, a little bit of context — holiday promo bumped usage last month.
[00:25] Maya: Perfect, Tom do you have the peak token counts?
[00:30] Tom: Yeah, so token volume is up about 42% MoM, embeddings are up 30%, cost per 1M tokens rose slightly because we hit more p99 tails and a lot of small requests that don't batch well.
[00:40] Diego: Right, small single-turn calls kill batching efficiency, we noticed similar. We can suggest continuous batching and some client-side bundling for those microcalls.
[00:47] Aisha: On the reliability side we had that incident on 03/01 where a region failover caused retries and some 500s, we lost around 20 minutes of throughput.
[00:55] Maya: I saw that, Priya can you run through the incident postmortem?
[01:00] Priya: Briefly — load balancer misconfig and a routing flap during a deploy, Redwood's fallback routed some traffic to the secondary model variant which added latency but kept the calls alive. We kicked off a fix same day and error rates are back to baseline.
[01:15] Carla: Was there any data exposure or logs that we should be worried about?
[01:18] Priya: No data exposure, audit logs look clean, we rotated keys as a precaution, and we'll share the full security timeline in the pack.
[01:25] Maya: On costs, Tom you mentioned small requests — we typically recommend batching and prefix caching, plus the quantized model variants for chat completions to lower unit cost.
[01:34] Tom: We're worried about quality impact if we quantize, customers notice hallucination upticks sometimes.
[01:38] Diego: Understandable — our suggestion is A/B the quantized model on a fraction of traffic and run evals on your prompt set. Often the 4-bit quant gives 20-30% cost savings with minimal delta on the evals.
[01:50] Aisha: Can Redwood run that A/B for us or do we need dedicated infra?
[01:53] Diego: We can run the initial A/B in hosted, but for sustained load and to measure p99 latency we recommend a dedicated pool or private pilot. That gives you consistent concurrency and avoids noisy neighbor effects.
[02:05] Carla: What's the delta in latency if we move to dedicated? We worry about provisioning time and cost.
[02:10] Maya: Dedicated typically tightens p95/p99 by 10-25% because of reserved GPUs and tuned kernels; cost is higher upfront but unit cost per token can drop if you have sustained volumes.
[02:19] Tom: If we do a one-month pilot on private deployment, what does Redwood need from us?
[02:23] Priya: Minimal: network connectivity (VPC peering or transit), sample prompt set, and a small dataset for evals. We'll provide a checklist and SOW.
[02:33] Aisha: Security approvals are on our side — we need SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration details.
[02:38] Maya: I'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:42] Tom: About the 03/01 incident — any mitigation to prevent region failover pain? We can't have retries spike costs.
[02:49] Diego: Two levers — multi-region sticky routing and better circuit-breaker policies at the client. Also model fallback to a lighter model variant rather than re-queueing requests.
[02:58] Tom: Ok we'll share the client logs for the retry pattern.
[03:02] Maya: Great, action items on sharing logs and Redwood running a benchmark. Let's talk specifics on the benchmark — Diego?
[03:08] Diego: We'll run p50/p95/p99 on your prompt set, measure tokens/sec and tail latency with both hosted and dedicated configs. We'll include caching on/off and quantized vs FP16. Expect an initial report within 5 business days after we get the data.
[03:22] Carla: Any concerns about data residency for the pilot? Some customers in EU need data to stay in-region.
[03:27] Priya: We can pin the region for pilot, or run a private deployment in their EU region; audit logs and KMS stay in-region as part of the option.
[03:35] Aisha: One more on cost — can you show us the cost sensitivity if we change batching window and model size?
[03:40] Maya: Yes, Priya will send a pricing sensitivity worksheet that models tokens/sec, batching windows, and different quant profiles.
[03:47] Tom: For the bench we also want to measure cold start times for model variants when the KV cache is cold. That influenced our earlier SLAs.
[03:54] Diego: We'll include cold-start scenarios and KV cache warmup curves. Also measure throughput for prefix caching so you see the marginal benefit.
[04:02] Aisha: Any legal/compliance blockers we should know? Procurement asked if Redwood supports SAML SSO and role-based access.
[04:08] Maya: Yes, SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported; Priya will share the doc with exact configuration steps.
[04:13] Carla: What's the expected timeline to move from pilot to dedicated if pilot looks good?
[04:17] Maya: Typically 6-12 weeks depending on procurement and infra, shorter if you already have reserved capacity commitments.
[04:24] Tom: We'll fast-track procurement if the numbers look good.
[04:28] Priya: I'll put together the SOW and pilot checklist and loop in legal.
[04:32] Maya: Ok let's recap, we have: Tom to share logs and traces by Friday, Diego to run benchmarks after we get data, Priya to send pricing and security pack, Maya to send SOC2 and KMS notes.
[04:44] Aisha: That matches our notes, thanks everyone.
[04:47] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with dates and invite for the benchmark runs.
[04:51] Carla: Bye all.
[04:53] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[04:55] (call ended)
